description: Two signals woven into one, in 2HP, by one of three rules deciding moment to moment which of them comes out

params.text: Sets the one figure the chosen rule uses: a breakpoint in U/L, a bias added to B in A>B, a minimum slope in R/F
Attenuates and inverts the parameter CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Chooses the rule: U/L takes A while it is above the breakpoint, A>B takes A while it exceeds B plus the bias, R/F takes A while it is rising or steady after a rise
Sets the span the breakpoint is read over in U/L mode, -5V to 5V or 0V to 10V; the other two rules ignore it

inputs.text: Moves the parameter, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim; a polyphonic signal here gives each channel its own parameter
The first of the two signals, and the one the rule tests
The second signal, taken whenever the rule turns away from A

outputs.text: Carries A or B moment to moment, each channel decided on its own
Carries a high gate while A is the one coming out, or while B is, according to the menu; a red mark beside it shows the second of those

notes: in R/F mode a saw is a poor choice for A, since a falling saw only counts as rising on the single sample where it jumps back to the top
with nothing patched into B, A>B mode compares A against the parameter voltage alone and puts out that voltage whenever A falls short
menu: High gate: On A selected (default), On B selected — chooses which of the two the gate output marks
Quantize mode — rounds the output to the nearest step of the size chosen, from a twelfth of a volt up to 5V, and is Off unless you set it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
